shortDescription: Stacks up to 7 playable z-levels (3 up / 3 down) into ONE banded RimWorld Map joined by synthetic RegionLink wormholes, so hauling, needs, work and storage come free from vanilla. Four vanilla-matched per-level sizes (126/190/250/300) and level counts are bought from a fixed 192,000-cell budget. Per-colony climate bands make high levels genuinely alpine. Content on lower levels draws smaller once per level of drop, which is what makes a deep column read as depth.
body:
> **NOTE TO SELF:** running spec, not a changelog. §1-19 architecture; §20 compat; §21-27 bug records. Keep every ⚠ - each cost a run to learn.

# As above, So below II (V2)

> V1 is DELETED. ~72 files, ~20,800 LOC. No em-dashes anywhere in shipped text.

## Pitch
Up to seven z-levels in ONE RimWorld `Map`. Priorities: (1) visual clarity from above, (2) performance, (3) vanilla parity.

## Status
Visuality, QOL, altitude/weather, settings VERIFIED. **250 tier VERIFIED (#236); 190x5 VERIFIED (#237-#240).**
**✅ §24b VERIFIED IN PLAY (#240): rock renders at every level, with Better Mountains installed.**
**✅ §24c VERIFIED IN PLAY (#248, vanilla / no BM): mass interiors solid, no pinhole grid.**
**🔧 §27 FIXED, UNVERIFIED: below-snow smoothing kernel ignored neighbour VISIBILITY, so snow held full opacity against rocky peaks and faded only in the interior.** First real below-snow finding - §6f had never been exercised on a cold map until #248.
**🔧 §25 FIXED, UNVERIFIED: §21's fog-on-reload AND the doubled/inverted stairs are ONE bug in `ABSkySync`.** A repair sweep ships with it for already-damaged saves.
UNVERIFIED: §25, §27, depth shrink, camera anchor, §18 audit, reroll grid, VEE compat, GL roof fix.

**PUBLISHED-BUILD BUGS.** 1. Preview 190-only - **FIXED** (§6d-CLAMP). 2. Fog/rocks on reload - **FIXED, see §25** (was §21, HELD for months). 3. GL rivers - **TABLED with a contradiction** (§22). 4. MO formations 4x overlapping - **FIXED** (§24a). 5. Rock visible only one level down - **FIXED + VERIFIED** (§24b). 6. Stairs invert and double on reload - **FIXED, same root cause as #2** (§25). 7. Rounded-corner holes through below mass, non-BM only - **FIXED + VERIFIED** (§24c). 8. Below-snow fade inverted at rocky peaks - **FIXED** (§27).

---

# 1. ARCHITECTURE
One `Map`, size `(w, 1, bandCount * Slot)`. Bands stack along +z from the deepest basement, gutter between. `Slot = ceil((bandHeight + MinGutter)/64)*64`; **64-alignment of SLOT is load-bearing** (terrain shaders sample by world position).

**The one insight.** `Region.Neighbors` is *topological, not spatial*. Wormhole `RegionLink`s between one-cell `RegionType.Portal` ends conduct connectivity without merging rooms, temperature or vacuum, and `Reachability.CanReach` works unpatched. But reachability is not a path: 1.6's pathfinder is jobified and cannot traverse a synthetic link, hence segmented movement (§3).

**Hard 1.6 constraints.** Path grid is IJobParallelFor over EVERY cell, so total stacked cells is the runtime metric. No `PathFinder.FindPath`. `BlocksDiagonalMovement` trips on unwalkable cells.

**⚠ The stack is 2x to 7x anisotropic.** Anything vanilla normalises by BOTH dimensions is distorted - a bug class that cannot appear on a square map.

### ⚠ THE SLICING RULE, seven shapes
| Shape | Example | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Anchor, a fraction of `Size.z` | river/lake centre; random/edge cell; VEE Crater jitter | remap the point |
| Field, a gradient on map centre | coastline (§6e); VEE LoneIsland and Crater | re-centre the sample coordinate |
| Noise space, a slice is not a short map | Map Preview (§6d); GL landform grids (§22) | generate at full height, then crop |
| Distance-to-extent, a margin off `Size` | `CloseToEdge`, no-build edge; river WIDTH | re-base onto the cell's band rect |
| **Aspect ratio, normalised by BOTH dims** | preview window and reroll grid (§6d) | lay out from the BAND, generate at the STACK |
| **Map-wide scalar** | snow melt (§7), temperature readout (§16), GL roof sweep | rewrite it per cell at the consumer |
| **Foreign absolute writes** (§22) | GL landform output lands in band 0, our carve overwrites it | ORDER, not arithmetic |

Still unaudited: Basin, Cavern, Chasm, Cliffs, Hollow, Valley (all `FalloffAtAngle`).
**`ABBandLocal.cs` is THE canonical FIELD rewrite** plus `BandLocalModule`, a `ModuleBase` wrapper for direct noise samplers.

# 2. LEVEL PLAN, budget 192,000 cells
**⚠ THE 64 CONSTRAINT IS ON *SLOT*, NOT BAND HEIGHT.** The original tiers were all 64k-2 - the tightest fit - and **that coincidence was mistaken for the requirement for months**.

| size | slot | gutter | cells/band | playable | max levels | total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 126 | 128 | 2 | 16,128 | 98.4% | 7 (cap) | 112,896 |
| 190 | 192 | 2 | 36,480 | 99.0% | 5 | 182,400 ✅ |
| **250** | 256 | 6 | 64,000 | 97.7% | 3 | **192,000** ✅ |
| **300** | 320 | 20 | 96,000 | 93.8% | 2 | **192,000** |

250/300 are vanilla's Medium and Large exactly. **Budget is tuned:** 192,000 = `3 x 64,000` = `2 x 96,000`. Ladder 7/5/3/2; 350/382 not offered because a second level exceeds the whole budget.
**⚠ 200 IS THE ONE NUMBER TO AVOID** - just past the 192 boundary: slot 256, gutter 56, 21.9% wasted. **Waste is a SAWTOOTH.**
**⚠ A WIDE GUTTER IS A FEATURE** - "a spatial helper that reaches 22 rows will cross a 2-row gutter" is the root of §15a and §4.
**Old saves are safe** - `bandHeight` is scribed; `SlotFor` is generic. **`Size.x == bandHeight` is a repair tool.**
**⚠ THE PLAN PERSISTS BETWEEN COLONIES AND SILENTLY CONSTRAINS THE SIZE.** Levels must be reduced BEFORE a larger size is selectable. Read the PLAN line before believing any size test.
**⚠ Own the widget, do not patch the data.** Our radio buttons write `GameInitData.mapSize` directly - **the authoritative record of the choice.** **Adding a tier means growing the `InitialSize` postfix** (now +288f). **The chooser LATCHES global state, released in a `Finalizer`.**

# 3-5. MOVEMENT, ORDERING, DESCENT
**Cross-band movement** segmented at ONE interception; hops must strictly decrease. **Multi-hop UNTESTED IN PLAY.**
**Group ordering:** the drag line between bands runs through the GUTTER; the odd/even signature ("3 and 5 fail, 2 and 4 do not") is the proof - only ODD counts sample exactly 0.5.
**⚠ ONE DESCENT RULE: `TryResolveVisibleBelow`.** TEN systems share it. **NINE appearances of the single-step bug** - eight as `- Slot` arithmetic, **the ninth (§24b) as a TERRAIN-DEF GATE with no arithmetic in it at all**, invisible to the standing grep audit. **`TryResolveVisibleFrom` is THE gate.**
**⚠ AND THE GATE ANSWERS TWO QUESTIONS, NOT ONE** (§27): *which* level a cell shows, and *whether* it shows anything. A consumer that resolves the centre and then reads raw grids for the neighbours has silently answered only the first.

# 6. SKY-MASS PRESENTATION
Despeckle (walls dissolve only at 7+ open neighbours; at 6 it ate the outermost wall row off every meadow edge), central fog hole, five-terrain plateau palette, cliff faces, alpine pass.
**⚠ The mass tapers with altitude, so +3 may contain NO LAND AT ALL.** Quantified (#237): surface 12,723 plants / fertility 0.631; +1 248 / 0.069; +2 170 / 0.046; +3 **37 / 0.012**.
**⚠ THE SKY BAND'S OWN MASS IS `AB_MountainTop` TERRAIN AND NOTHING ELSE IDENTIFIES IT.** `ABSkyBandGen` writes it for `KindLedge` (no edifice, no roof) and `KindWall` (rock edifice + `RoofRockThick`). A `KindLedge` cell is indistinguishable by terrain from a DERIVED mountain top, which is why `ABSkySync` may now only create `AB_MountainTop`, never overwrite one (§25).
**Snow-holding, and it decides where snow fades:** `AB_OpenAir` and `AB_WallTop` set `holdSnowOrSand=false`; **`AB_MountainTop` and `AB_RoofSurface` do NOT and therefore hold snow.** A `KindWall` cell still stays bare because its rock edifice is Full fillage and `SnowGrid.CanHaveSnow` rejects it. So vanilla's own snow layer fades correctly on a sky band unaided - which is what proved §27 was ours.

# 6a. ⚠ THE BELOW VIEW IS MIRRORED PASSES, NOT ONE RENDERER
`SectionLayer_ABBelowV2` ports vanilla `SectionLayer_Terrain` **and nothing else**. Confirmed five times: Water (§6b), Snow (§6f), **mass sprites (§24b)**, **linked corner fillers (§24c)**, **snow's visibility kernel (§27)**.
**⚠ THE CONVERSE IS HANDLED.** A foreign `Thing.Print` postfix prints into OUR layer and is still correct, because the call is bracketed `SnapshotVertCounts()` -> `Print` -> `FinishNewVerts`, and **`FinishNewVerts` transforms by VERTEX RANGE**. Preserve that.
**⚠ THREE DIFFERENT THINGS ARE ALL CALLED "MASS", AND THEY ARE REPRESENTED DIFFERENTLY.** This distinction cost three failed fixes (§24b):
| what | representation | drawn by |
|---|---|---|
| undug GROUND mountain | a real rock **edifice**, but FOGGED so its sprite is never printed | cap, from one Slot up |
| SKY-band mass | `AB_MountainTop` **terrain**, NO edifice at all | cap, into that band's own mesh |
| mined-out floor | rock leave-**terrain** | `ABMinedRockLookup` |
**Any code that tests only `edificeGrid` misses sky mass entirely; any code that tests only terrain misses undug ground.**
**⚠ THE CAP IS SINGLE-STEP.** `SectionLayer_ABMountainCap` derives from `-bands.Slot`, exactly one band down. Correct for a sky band's own tapering mass; the cost is that nothing else drew mass deeper than one slot until §24b.
**Ascent rule:** the dirty mirror stops at the first opaque floor, tested over the cell and its eight neighbours; the FIRST step stays unconditional *because* the cap is single-step.
**⚠ THE UNIT OF WASTE IS A SECTION REGENERATION, NOT A CELL.**
**⚠ VISIBILITY IS DECIDED ENTIRELY BY `ABBands.ShowsBelow(terrain)`, SO A TERRAIN SWAP IS A RENDERING BUG.** `AB_WallTop` and `AB_OpenAir` are see-through; `AB_MountainTop` and `AB_RoofSurface` are opaque. Anything that rewrites one into the other silently changes what the whole below stack draws - that is §25.
**⚠ A SMOOTHING KERNEL IS A SECOND CONSUMER OF THAT SAME RULE** (§27). Any mirrored pass that averages over neighbours - snow today, and any future AO / edge / blend pass - must apply `ShowsBelow` to every sample, not only to the cell it is colouring.

# 6b-6g. WATER, PREVIEW, COASTS, SNOW, SHRINK
**Water** is TWO-PASS SCREEN-SPACE; `SectionLayer_ABBelowWatergen` targets `SubcameraDefOf.WaterDepth.LayerId`. Rivers remap `GetRiverCenter` (not `Init`); `GetLakeCenter` needs the same or it undoes the first. Width clamped at the producer. **⚠ ALL THREE INERT UNDER GL** (§22).
**⚠ 6d-CLAMP, PUBLISHED BUG:** `Stacked()` ran the incoming size through `Clamp()`, which returns *the largest offered size ≤ input that fits*. Map Preview passes VANILLA's size (250 default), so `Clamp(250)` returned 190 **regardless of the player's pick**. **Fix: `PlannedSize`** - the chooser already wrote the answer to `GameInitData.mapSize`.
**⚠ MAP PREVIEW SHIPS IN TWO HALVES AND GL BUNDLES ONE.** With GL installed and Map Preview absent, `Active` is TRUE while window types are ABSENT. **Do not "simplify" `Active`.**
**6d-REROLL:** the window opened EMPTY - `elementSize.y = 403/126*896 = 2,866 px` -> `gridSize.y = 0` -> `DesiredCount = 0`.
**Coasts:** CENTRED wrong, not scaled wrong. NO SCALING. **⚠ "None override `GetNoiseValue`" is about VANILLA ONLY.**
**6f. Below-snow:** no mirror of `SectionLayer_Snow` existed; the layer that fixed that had **never run on a cold map** until #248, and its first exposure produced §27. Geometry is built ONCE and only colours are rewritten - **never `ClearSubMeshes(All)` here**, or the colour count stops matching the vertex count. Every cell must emit exactly nine colours including invisible ones, or all later cells shift onto the wrong vertices.
**Depth shrink (UNVERIFIED):** **⚠ the atlas trap** - past `ZoomRootSize` 18 humanlikes render from a cached atlas blit ignoring `PawnDrawParms.matrix`. **⚠ natural rock excluded BY DEF, not by link type**, because BM makes rock non-linked.
**⚠ PERSPECTIVE MODE WAS BUILT AND REMOVED. Do not re-add as polish.**

# 7-8a. CHARACTER, CAMERA
Ore `x(1+0.45*(depth-1))` scales `basementOreDensity` through our OWN `ABOreGen.ScatterOres`. **⚠ The snow line never worked, and the comment saying it did not need to was wrong.**
**The camera clamp and level-switch input share `ABGuard.Camera`**, both per-frame paths where an unthrottled `Log.Error` turns a cosmetic bug into a hang.
**New-game anchor:** only `StartedNewGame` runs after vanilla's own camera jump. ⚠ OPEN: `z=24` was EXACTLY `PodScatterMargin`.

# 9. GENERATION COST

## 9a. The profile stamps its own conditions
Prints `TILE`, `PLAN`, `SCOPING:`, two censuses. Has voided or explained SEVEN comparisons - **#248 was voided by its own TILE line (hilliness Flat) before a single pixel was examined.** **⚠ THE WATER REPORT DOES NOT AND SHOULD.**

## 9b. ⚠ "COST IS DESTRUCTION NOT GENERATION" - NO LONGER TRUE, AND THE FIX IS WHY
#188 was 16/84. #231 is 71/29. Rock suppression worked, so the carve got cheap and cost moved to generation. **A historical record of a fixed problem.**

## 9c-9f. Measured cost curve, six tiles
| run | plan | tile | gensteps | carve | total | destroyed | suppressed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| #231 | 7x126 | Flat TropSwamp | 3,836 | 1,580 | ~5.7 s | 4,575 | 1,627 |
| #236 | 3x250 | SmallHills | 5,001 | **7,118** | ~12.4 s | 15,611 | 7,272 |
| #237 | 5x190 | Mountainous | 4,529 | 2,201 | ~6.9 s | 7,497 | 85,304 |
| #238 | 5x190 | SmallHills | 3,389 | 4,718 | ~8.3 s | 16,100 | 11,175 |
| #239 | 5x190 | Mountainous Desert | 2,217 | 2,357 | **~4.7 s** | 7,906 | 76,702 |
| #248 | 5x190 | **Flat** Tundra | 2,108 | 3,282 | ~5.4 s | 12,103 | 5,689 |

**⚠ FillRock is SUPERLINEAR in band size:** 190 -> 36,480 cells -> ~1,046-2,200 ms; 250 -> 64,000 cells -> 4,254 ms. **1.75x cells, 2.87x time**, exactly as the `ListerThings` linear-`List.Remove` mechanism predicts.
**⚠ HILLINESS DECIDES THE BILL.** #237 vs #238 is a clean control - same tier, plan and biome, only hilliness differs - and the mountainous map SUPPRESSES 85,304 rocks while the small-hills map DESTROYS 16,100. Suppression is the cheap path.
**⚠ AND HILLINESS ALSO DECIDES WHETHER A RENDERING TEST IS VALID AT ALL** (#248). A Flat tile spawns no mass wide enough to have mask-15 interior cells, so it can neither confirm nor refute a mass-rendering fix. **Read the TILE line before reading the screenshot.**
**⚠ THE 250 TIER IS THE EXPENSIVE ONE** (~12.4 s vs ~4.7-8.3 s at 190). I recommended the 192,000 budget reasoning about PATHFINDING and did not predict generation time would double.

## 9g. ⚠ RE-RANKED ON EVIDENCE, AGAINST MY OWN EARLIER ADVICE
`GenStep_Plants` across six tiles: **2,270 / 2,225 / 1,086 / 1,326 / 61.5 / 464 ms** - a **37x spread**, dominated by rainfall (Desert rain 378 -> 61.5 ms; Tundra rain 144 -> 464 ms; TropicalSwamp rain 2693 -> 2,270 ms).
I made four successive wrong claims about this one number: *"84% is grown then erased"* (false - the `DESTROYED by def` census in the same log shows no plant def in the top ten; the cost is the SCAN, not wasted placement), *"biome-independent"* (dead at n=3), *"tracks hilliness"* (dead at n=4), *"1.1-2.3 s"* (dead at n=5).
**Basement `FillRock` is 1,046-4,254 ms on EVERY tile.** Tile-independent beats tile-dependent, so:
1. **Basement rock suppression** - consistently 1.0-4.3 s. **Now item 1.**
2. **`GenStep_Plants` traversal scoping** - 0.06-2.3 s, worthless on desert, ~2 s on wet flat. **Demoted.**
3. **`GenStep_RockChunks`** - `Filth_RubbleRock` is the top destroyed def on all six tiles.
4. Scattered ruins (also a CONTENT BUG). 5. Perlin precompute (changes determinism).

# 10-12. PERF AND DIAGNOSTICS
59.6 fps at 96 pawns. **⚠ THAT BENCHMARK MEASURES THE WRONG THING** - cost is in section-regeneration BURSTS.
**⚠ Bisect toggles PERSIST across runs.** Now STAMPED INTO THE PROFILE.
**⚠ The pre-pinned palette always strips its LAST entry. n=7.** Keep padding with a DISTINCT throwaway.
**⚠ THE AUTO-PROMPT IS EDGE-TRIGGERED, SO CHECK THE COUNT, NOT THE TEXT.** `monitor_get_error` returns the LATEST occurrence, which may be the FIRST - byte-identical and stale.
**⚠ OUR OWN PROFILE ARRIVES AS A `warning` ROW ATTRIBUTED TO US.** It is deliberate (info level is filtered out of the bridge), so a run that reports "1 new error class" and nothing else is a CLEAN run. Read it for TILE/PLAN before concluding anything about the test.
**⚠ Debug actions are `AllowedGameStates.PlayingOnMap`** - silently inert on the world map / preview screen.
**⚠ AUDIT A DIAGNOSTIC'S OWN FILTERS BEFORE TRUSTING A NEGATIVE.** The below-layer report filtered on `StartsWith("SectionLayer_ABBelow")`, which excluded `SectionLayer_ABMountainCap` - a layer that draws into the below view. **A missing row and an empty row are indistinguishable**, and the omission nearly cleared the guilty layer. Now `SectionLayer_AB`.

# 13. OPEN WORK
1. **VERIFY §27** (cold map, stand on a sky band, look at snow meeting a rocky peak: the fade should land at the rock silhouette, no cell-aligned rectangles) and **§25** on the reporter's save.
2. **Basement rock suppression** (§9g item 1).
3. Verify tiers 126/300; preview at 300; §18 audit; VEE compat; GL roof fix; reroll grid; depth shrink; camera anchor.
4. Stamp TILE/PLAN into the water report.
5. §9g items 2-5; audit the other `FalloffAtAngle` mutators.
6. **Never exercised:** multi-hop stair router, elevator, basement PATHING/wormholes, cavern basement.
7. `ShotReport` drops target size. Biomes! at 40%. Better Trees unexamined (§23c). **Store page still says three levels.**
8. **§22 TABLED** - do not resume without re-reading the contradiction.
9. **CAI 5000 fog of war is a standing save-corruption risk we do not control** (§26). Only pursue if fog persists after §25.

# 14. LESSONS
**Method.** Prove a subsystem innocent by finding a state where the suspect CANNOT EXIST. Re-open a rejection only by naming the confound. Change one thing per experiment. Run the diagnostic before the third theory. A beautiful fit is not evidence.
**⚠ CLEAR THE OTHER SUSPECT BY READING ITS DATA, NOT ITS CODE.** §27 was "is this vanilla's snow layer on the sky band, or our below-snow mirror?" One grep of our own terrain defs settled it: `AB_OpenAir`/`AB_WallTop` are `holdSnowOrSand=false` and a `KindWall` edifice is Full fillage, so vanilla's kernel already sees zeroes in exactly the right cells and fades correctly unaided. **A def field can exonerate a whole layer faster than reading either layer.**
**⚠ A FIX FOR MOD X CAN BE A REGRESSION FOR EVERYONE WITHOUT X, AND THE BRANCH IS WHERE TO LOOK.** §24c: the BM fix added ONE emitter with two halves, and only the BM half was exercised in play. **When a fix lands as `if (foreignShape) A else B`, the untested branch is B, on the majority configuration.** Verify the fix on a vanilla load too, not only on the reporter's.
**⚠ REPRODUCING A SUBSYSTEM MEANS REPRODUCING ALL OF IT, NOT ITS MAIN OUTPUT.** An atlas tile is HALF of `Graphic_LinkedCornerFiller`; the quarter-cell fillers that cover the baked corner rounding are the other half. Drawing tiles alone gives a pillow grid with dark diamonds at every four-cell junction - "corners on the inner bound, it looks like holes". **Diff the new emitter against the working one line by line.**
**⚠ A COMMENT THAT JUSTIFIES SKIPPING ONE CHECK CAN BE HIDING A SECOND CHECK IT NEVER MENTIONS.** §27's kernel carried a well-argued paragraph explaining why it does not re-resolve the DESCENT per neighbour - correct, and it quietly stood in for the missing VISIBILITY test too. **Two questions collapsed into one justified answer.** When a comment defends an omission, name every question the omitted call would have answered.
**⚠ AN EVENT HOOK THAT LOOKS INCREMENTAL MAY BE A FULL-MAP SWEEP ON THE LOAD PATH.** `Building.SpawnSetup` calls `edificeGrid.Register` **without consulting `respawningAfterLoad`**, so every hook on it runs for EVERY building on EVERY load. `ABSkySync` was written as "event-driven, not scanned" and was in fact re-deriving the entire sky band from scratch each load (§25). **Before trusting "this only fires on change", ask what the LOAD path does.**
**⚠ TWO RESOLVERS FOR ONE QUANTITY IS A BUG WITH A DELAY FUSE.** `ABSkyBandGen` and `ABSkySync` both answer "what terrain belongs above this cell" and disagreed on one rule. Generation ran first and looked right; the load sweep ran later and silently rewrote the map into a shape generation would never produce. **When you add a live updater beside a generator, make one call the other or diff them line by line.**
**⚠ A FIX APPLIED TO ONE CASE MUST BE CARRIED TO ITS SIBLING CASE, AND THE COMMENT PROVES IT WAS NOT.** `ABSkySync`'s header proudly documented "ROOF BEATS EDIFICE" - and only the CONSTRUCTED-roof branch was ordered that way. **A confidently-written comment about a rule is where to look for the half of the rule that is missing.**
**⚠ READ THE GUARD CLAUSES OF THE HELPER YOU ARE ABOUT TO REUSE - INCLUDING YOUR OWN.** §24b attempt 1 routed through `EmitMassSilhouetteAt` after reading only its SIGNATURE. Its body opens with three early returns, each of which independently disabled the fix.
**⚠ ASK HOW THE SUBSYSTEM REPRESENTS THE THING, NOT WHAT THE THING IS.** §24b attempt 2 assumed "mass" always means a rock edifice. Sky mass is `AB_MountainTop` TERRAIN with no edifice; undug ground mass is an edifice whose sprite is fogged; a mined floor is leave-terrain.
**⚠ THE USER'S REPHRASING IS DATA.** "lower level textures disappear" and "+2 does not show the rock ledge of +1" describe the same screen but different mechanisms.
**⚠ A DIRECTIONAL WORD IN A REPORT IS A GRADIENT, AND GRADIENTS COME FROM KERNELS.** "fades INWARD instead of OUTWARD" is not a colour bug or a material bug; it says a weighted average is being fed the wrong samples. **Go straight to whatever averages over neighbours.**
**⚠ TWO SYMPTOMS REPORTED IN ONE BREATH ARE PROBABLY ONE BUG.** "Fog returns on reload" and "stairs invert and double" were the SAME line of code, because both are downstream of `ShowsBelow(terrain)`. **Ask what single quantity both symptoms read.**
**⚠ A SCREENSHOT CARRIES TERRAIN IDENTITY IF YOU KNOW YOUR OWN DEFS.** The grey tiled floor is `AB_RoofSurface`; the dark 2x2 behind the stairs is `AirMaskMat`. §24c added: **shrunken sprites are a DEPTH READOUT** - the small tree said drop/slot = 2, which picked the fogged `drop > slot` emitter out of three candidates. §27 added: **hard, cell-aligned rectangles at a light/dark boundary mean a per-cell alpha written without its neighbours' agreement** - vanilla's own layers never produce a square edge, because every one of them smooths over a nine-vertex fan.
**⚠ AUDIT A DIAGNOSTIC'S OWN FILTERS BEFORE TRUSTING A NEGATIVE.** See §12.
**⚠ CHECK THAT YOUR CONFIGURATION CAN EXPRESS THE DIFFERENCE BEFORE RUNNING THE EXPERIMENT.** #231's water report was clean and **worthless as a discriminator**; #248's Flat tile was the same mistake in map form.
**⚠ A CENSUS BEATS A MAGNITUDE - AND I IGNORED MY OWN RULE.**
**⚠ n=2 IS NOT A PATTERN, AND NEITHER IS n=4.** On a multi-factor quantity, report the RANGE and stop naming drivers.
**⚠ TILE-INDEPENDENT WINS BEAT TILE-DEPENDENT ONES.** Rank by worst case across conditions, not by the best measurement you happen to have.
**⚠ Measure the ratio before optimising the half you assumed - and RE-measure after.**
**⚠ A FIX CAN BE CHEAPER THAN THE BUG.** §27 replaced 289 gate calls + 8-per-visible-cell raw reads with 361 cached ones over a one-cell apron. **When a per-cell test has to become a per-neighbour test, cache the apron rather than accepting the 9x.**
**⚠ THE SYMPTOM SET IS ITSELF EVIDENCE.** §21 named fog AND rocks and nothing else, and I read that as "flat per-cell arrays sized by `map.Area`" - a mechanism that fit perfectly and was wrong. **A symptom pair narrows the search; it does not pick between two mechanisms that both explain it.**
**⚠ A LOSSY NORMALISER IS NOT A WAY TO READ A CHOICE.**
**⚠ A CONSTRAINT SATISFIED BY EVERY EXAMPLE IS NOT NECESSARILY THE CONSTRAINT.**
**⚠ A RULE ENFORCED BY GREPPING A SYNTAX ONLY CATCHES THAT SYNTAX.**
**⚠ A DESIGN CHOICE RECORDED WITHOUT ITS COST WILL BE READ AS FREE.**
**⚠ THE REAL CONFLICT IS USUALLY A REPLACEMENT, NOT A COLLISION.**
**⚠ AND THE BUG AFTER THAT IS USUALLY A COLLABORATION.** When neither side is wrong, look at the ORDER.
**⚠ CHECK WHETHER IT IS ALREADY BUILT BEFORE BUILDING IT.** §24c arrived as "we need a soft reflection check for BM" - the branch already existed and was type-based, which is strictly better than a packageId probe. **The requested mechanism is a hypothesis about the cause, not the cause.**
**⚠ A SHARED METHOD NAME IS A HYPOTHESIS, NOT A CONFLICT.** False-positive rate 50%; ReGrowth cleared four times.
**⚠ Compat work is mostly deletion.** **⚠ Design for the foreign patch you have not met.** **⚠ Waste is often a sawtooth.** **⚠ The thing you rounded away may be load-bearing.** **⚠ Duplication is how an invariant dies.** **⚠ A comment is not an invariant.** **⚠ Steady-state fps hides burst cost.** **⚠ Timing that reads exactly 0.0 ms is an early return.** **⚠ In a foreign log, the loudest error is usually downstream.** **⚠ A finding scoped to vanilla does not transfer to mods.**
**Patching.** Re-aim the shared parameter. Find the ONE virtual everything funnels through - and when there is none, **wrap the DATA instead of the reader**. Patch the PRODUCER, not the store. Own the widget. Never put a foreign type in a patch signature - type `__instance` as `object`. **Suppress the callee, not the caller.** **Prefix state is released in a Finalizer.** **Repair a foreign method's output rather than reimplementing it.** **Never clamp a Def field to fix one map.** **Prefer a published ExtensionPoint over racing internals.** **Read the LIVE def field, never a baked copy, when a mod can rewrite it at runtime.** **When a helper returns bool, use its return as the hand-off signal rather than duplicating its guards** (§24b).
**Engine facts.** `holdSnowOrSand` defaults TRUE, and **`SnowGrid.CanHaveSnow` rejects a cell on EITHER a `holdSnowOrSand=false` terrain OR a Full-fillage edifice** - two independent gates. **`SectionLayer_Snow` builds ONE nine-vertex-per-cell solid grid via `SectionLayerGeometryMaker_Solid.MakeBaseGeometry` and then rewrites only COLOURS, depth in the alpha channel; iteration is x-outer/z-inner and every cell must emit exactly nine colours or all later cells shift.** Its `vertexWeights[8]` is `{8}` (centre-only) and `GenAdj.AdjacentCellsAndInsideForUV[8]` is the cell itself - that pairing is what makes snow fade outward from a cell centre. Vanilla falls back to the CENTRE depth for out-of-bounds neighbours, so snow never fades against the map edge. Draw order is material render QUEUE, not altitude. `Banded` is FALSE for all of map generation. `SectionLayer` subclasses auto-discovered on EVERY map. FinalizeInit runs on a worker thread - generation latches must be `[ThreadStatic]`. Ore defs have no `naturalTerrain` **and no `_Rough` terrain at all**, so any code typing a cell from its edifice must fall back to the host stone beside it. `CameraJumper.TryJump` and `MapDrawer.MapMeshDirty` return silently unless `ProgramState == Playing`. Humanlikes past `ZoomRootSize` 18 render from an atlas blit ignoring `PawnDrawParms.matrix`. **Gensteps run with live-map bookkeeping DEFERRED (~40x cheaper than after `FinalizeInit`).** Harmony skips POSTFIXES when the original throws but always runs FINALIZERS; **a prefix returning false skips the original but POSTFIXES STILL RUN**; prefix and transpiler compose. **`FogGrid` is a `NativeBitArray` in 1.6, scribed via `DataExposeUtility.LookBitArray`; both it and `MapFileCompressor` save/load CORRECTLY at any map size (audited, §25).** **`WaterInfo.GetWaterMovement` indexes `x * map.Size.z + z`.** **TileMutatorDefs compete within a `categories` entry, so a mod can REPLACE a vanilla mutator.** **`ThingDef.graphic` is baked at PostLoad and never refreshed; `graphicData.Graphic` is lazily rebuilt from CURRENT graphicData.** **`subGraphic.MatSingle` of a linked graphic is the WHOLE atlas sheet.** **Every tile in a linked atlas has its four corners rounded away; `Graphic_LinkedCornerFiller` covers them with quarter-cell fillers at each corner whose diagonal AND both flanking cardinals link.** **Vanilla rock links with `MapEdge`, so off-map counts as LINKED.** **`Building.SpawnSetup` registers with the edifice grid unconditionally, including `respawningAfterLoad`.** **`Map.FinalizeInit` calls `MapComponentUtility.FinalizeInit` LAST, after `RebuildAllRegionsAndRooms`.** **`Building_Door.DrawMovers` draws the graphic TWICE, the second on `MeshPool.plane10Flip` - the one vanilla path that renders a doubled, mirrored sprite.**

# 24. MULTI-CELL AND MULTI-LEVEL MASS

## 24a. FIXED: MO formations drawn four times overlapping
`IsPrintAnchor` picks the first cell of a multi-cell thing whose viewing cell can see it - single-valued **only if every cell resolves to the same `drop`**. It does not. Four cells, four anchors, four quads at the same `TrueCenter`.
**Fixed by deduping per THING per Regenerate pass**, not by changing the anchor rule. **Never MO-specific.**

## 24b. ✅ FIXED AND VERIFIED (#240): rock renders at every level
**Root cause, three layers deep:** the cap derives from exactly one Slot down and draws into that band's own mesh; the below layer's bridge to it fired only for `def == AB_MountainTop`; and every cross-level path ran through `EmitMassSilhouetteAt`, which returns false for mineable edifices and non-linked graphics - i.e. for every rock under Better Mountains.
**Fix:** `SectionLayer_ABMountainCap.EmitMassRepresentationAt` draws the mass itself, reached two ways - `if (!EmitMassSilhouetteAt(...)) EmitMassRepresentationAt(...)` for unfogged sky ledges, and from the `foggedBelow` branch gated `drop > slot` for undug ground mountain. `MassRockAt` resolves both representations.
**⚠ THREE FAILED ATTEMPTS, AND THE PATTERN IS THE VALUE.** Each was the same error in a different place: assuming how a subsystem represents mass instead of checking.

## 24c. ✅ FIXED AND VERIFIED (#248): §24b's regression on vanilla - rounded corners read as holes
**Report:** "mineable rocks on the level below show corners on the inner bound, which makes it look like holes" - **only WITHOUT Better Mountains**, and only since the BM support shipped.
**Root cause.** `EmitMassRepresentationAt` has two halves. BM rock is `Graphic_Random` and returns in the VARIANT half (verified #240). Vanilla rock is `Graphic_Linked` and fell into the ATLAS half, which drew `SubMaterialFromAtlas(mask)` **and nothing else** - half of vanilla's drawer. Bare tiles across a mass interior produce a grid of pale pillows with a dark diamond at every four-cell junction. It also drew the mask-15 interior tile, which the cap's own in-band pass deliberately skips as near-flat.
**Which path, from the screenshot alone.** The tree in the shot was visibly shrunk, and depth shrink is `drop / slot` levels - so drop/slot = 2, which selects the FOGGED `drop > slot` emitter over the two unfogged candidates.
**Fix, three parts, all inside the atlas half:** corner fillers on the exact vanilla rule; mask 15 skipped when the rough-stone field was drawn; `MassLinked` replaces `IsMass` for the mask with off-map counting as LINKED. Plus the field falls back to the host stone's rough terrain when the cell's own def has none (**ore has no `naturalTerrain`**), which is what makes the mask-15 skip safe over an ore vein.

# 25. 🔧 FIXED (UNVERIFIED IN PLAY): ONE `ABSkySync` BUG, TWO PUBLISHED SYMPTOMS
**Reports:** (a) "on reloading a save, fog returns where it shouldn't be with open areas"; (b) "stair textures invert and start doubly". Different subsystems by description, ONE line of code in fact.

**The trigger, shared.** `Building.SpawnSetup` calls `map.edificeGrid.Register(this)` **without consulting `respawningAfterLoad`**. `Map.FinalizeLoading` respawns every building including every compressed `Mineable`, so `Patch_EdificeGrid_ABRegister` -> `ABSkySync.SyncAbove` re-derives the ENTIRE sky band on every load. Both symptoms are therefore reload-only, and both persist because the rewritten terrain is then saved - it compounds every load.

**(a) The fog blob - `AB_MountainTop` -> `AB_WallTop`.** `Resolve` tested *impassable edifice* before *natural roof*. Undug rock is an impassable edifice under a natural roof, so every cell above unmined surface rock resolved to `AB_WallTop`, while `ABSkyBandGen` had written `AB_MountainTop`. `AB_WallTop` is `dontRender` and `ShowsBelow`-true, so the sky band's mountain mass turned see-through and `EmitBelowFogFan` painted the SURFACE's fog through it. It also silently made that mass Impassable and left §24b's mass renderer with nothing to draw.

**(b) The doubled, inverted stairs - `AB_RoofSurface` -> `AB_OpenAir`.** `CarveLanding` writes `AB_RoofSurface` for a sky landing *after* `base.SpawnSetup` already ran the sync. `Resolve` sees an unroofed `Building_Door` (`PassThroughOnly`, not Impassable) and returns `AB_OpenAir`. The landing goes see-through with the link still standing in it, and `SectionLayer_ABBelowV2` prints the level below's stairwell into that cell on top of the real one. Up-art and down-art are vertical mirrors, hence "invert and start doubly".

**Fix, four parts.**
1. `Resolve` precedence is now constructed roof -> **natural roof** -> impassable edifice -> open air, matching `ABSkyBandGen` by construction.
2. `IsDerived` no longer contains `AB_MountainTop`. The rule is **one-way**: the sync may create a mountain top, never overwrite one.
3. `SyncAbove` bails when the target cell `CarriesOwnStructure`, and bails on the solid -> `AB_OpenAir` transition when `OnLinkLanding` finds a link within `ABWormholePather.LandingRadius`.
4. `ABSkySync.RepairAfterLoad`, called from `ABBandMap.FinalizeInit` - **deliberately placed there because that is the first moment the damage for THIS load has already happened.**

**⚠ THE REPAIR IS TWO NARROW TRANSITIONS, NOT A RE-DERIVE.** The two rules can only move a cell back to a state the generator itself produces: `AB_WallTop` over a NATURAL roof -> `AB_MountainTop`; and `AB_OpenAir` within a sky link's carved rect -> `AB_RoofSurface`, walked from the LINKS rather than by sweeping cells. Idempotent; logs a one-line count when it repairs anything.

# 27. 🔧 FIXED (UNVERIFIED): BELOW-SNOW FADED THE WRONG WAY AT ROCKY PEAKS
**Report (#248, first cold map to exercise §6f):** "snow on the upper level fades inward towards other snow covered tiles instead of outward toward the rocky peaks." Screenshot also showed hard, cell-aligned rectangles where snow met rock.

**Not vanilla's layer.** `AB_OpenAir`/`AB_WallTop` are `holdSnowOrSand=false` and a `KindWall` cell's rock edifice is Full fillage, so `SnowGrid.CanHaveSnow` already zeroes exactly the cells vanilla's kernel needs to fade against. Vanilla is correct on a sky band unaided.

**Root cause.** `SectionLayer_ABBelowSnow` resolved see-below visibility for the CENTRE cell, then sampled the nine-neighbour smoothing kernel straight out of `SnowGrid` at `z - drop`. A neighbour standing under a rocky peak is opaque from above, but its *lower-level* cell usually has snow - so the kernel read off-screen snow and held full opacity right up to the peak. The opaque cell meanwhile writes alpha 0 across all nine of its own vertices, giving the hard square edge. The only place alpha could ramp was the interior, wherever the level below happened to be bare: exactly "fades inward towards other snow covered tiles".

**Why it survived review.** The method carries a well-argued comment explaining why it deliberately does NOT re-resolve the DESCENT per neighbour (mixing two bands into one kernel would seam). That reasoning is correct and it quietly stood in for the VISIBILITY question, which nobody had asked. See §14.

**Fix.** A one-cell-apron visibility cache (`BuildVisibilityCache` / `VisibleAt`) built once per Regenerate from the shared gate. Three sample classes now, where there were two:
- outside the playable band (off map, or across the gutter at either end) -> **centre depth**, vanilla's map-edge rule, band-local, so no fade stripe grows along a band seam;
- inside the band but not visible from here (peak, ledge, roof, fogged) -> **zero**, so the fade lands on the silhouette of what is actually being looked at;
- visible -> sample at the centre's drop, unchanged.
**Cheaper than what it replaces:** 361 gate calls over the apron instead of 289 plus eight per visible cell.
